ai.description: This small toad reaches 35–45 mm. It is brown with darker dorsal markings and a pale belly. Key features include prominent triangular skin flaps above the eyes and a distinct, pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys minor* is best distinguished by its significantly smaller size and the presence of a distinct, slender "horn"-like dermal projection on each upper eyelid.
ai.habitat: The Little Horned Toad inhabits moist evergreen and subtropical broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Little Horned Toad is primarily nocturnal, remaining perfectly camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush passing insects during the night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys minor* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs in mountain streams. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys minor* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas and Northeast India (e.g., Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland) at elevations typically ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Megophrys minor* emits a sharp, metallic "tink" or "click" sound, repeated at regular intervals within the humid, high-altitude forest floor habitats it inhabits.
